title: feat: add chrome-headless-shell install and sandbox-friendly Chrome launching
description:
This PR lets nokap (and so `GT.gtsave()` in Great Tables) render inside macOS sandboxes such as mcp-console's Seatbelt profile, where full Chrome aborts at startup. A new opt-in `nokap install-chrome` command and `nokap.install_chrome()` function download chrome-headless-shell from Chrome for Testing into a per-user cache, and `find_chrome()` now prefers it over a system Chrome (`CHROME_PATH` still wins).

When the sandbox denies Chrome's mach service registration, `Chrome` relaunches once with `--single-process`, and a new `NOKAP_CHROME_ARGS` environment variable passes extra flags to any launch, including the one behind `gtsave()`. 

Launch failures now explain sandbox causes (a blocked localhost port, or full Chrome's SIGABRT), and `info`/`doctor report whether the browser is headless-shell. The PR also fixes `Chrome.__del__` raising `AttributeError` after a failed `__init__`, closes the Chrome process when a launch fails, and updates the installation, CLI, and error-handling guides.

title: Add explicit renderers and Chrome pipes for sandboxed rendering
description:
Allow nokap to render in sandboxes that block local TCP listeners and let integrations own their browser configuration and lifetime without changing process-wide environment variables. Pipes are the default on macOS and Linux; Windows continues to use WebSockets. With `chrome-headless-shell` installed, Great Tables can render inside MCP Console's macOS sandbox without manual Chrome flags or changes to sandbox permissions. `NOKAP_TRANSPORT` and explicit `transport=` arguments remain available; callers using `Chrome.port` or `Chrome.ws_url` must select WebSockets. Add `Renderer(path=None, *, headless=True, extra_args=None, timeout=20, transport=None)`. Each instance launches and owns a browser and CDP connection, reads its configuration at construction, and supports repeated captures through methods or the module functions: ```python with nokap.Renderer(extra_args=["--lang=de"]) as renderer: nokap.from_html("

Hello

", "hello.png", renderer=renderer) renderer.webshot("https://example.com", "page.png") ``` Module functions borrow an explicit renderer without closing it. Context exit or `renderer.close()` releases its resources; closing is terminal, and an explicit renderer does not silently replace an exited browser. Calls without `renderer=` share a default renderer, retaining automatic recreation. `nokap.close()` affects only that shared default. Both transports use separate temporary profiles unless a caller supplies `--user-data-dir`. On macOS, check the user and cache directory queries that Chrome needs to initialize its child-process sandboxes. If either query fails with `EIO`, select `--single-process` before launch: Chrome can otherwise exit before reporting a Mach registration error. Other query errors propagate, and explicit `--single-process` or `--no-sandbox` skips this check. The existing retry after a reported Mach registration denial remains in place. Internally, the pipe launcher passes inherited descriptors to Chrome and waits for a CDP response before reporting startup success. The pipe client handles command responses and events, including images larger than a pipe buffer. Renderer startup failures close partially acquired resources; normal cleanup closes the connection before the browser and removes its temporary profile. The CLI doctor reports the selected transport. Documentation covers configuration, ownership, batch reuse, and a Great Tables example in MCP Console. Native Pillow display in Console is covered separately by [posit-dev/mcp-console#225](https://github.com/posit-dev/mcp-console/pull/225).
